question.question: When a leader confirms a later queued ReadIndex context and releases an earlier remote request in the same prefix, does publication preserve the earlier request context and origin through the emitted reply and recipient readiness?
question.importance: Mis-correlated read results can retire leader-side pending work without notifying the originating local batch, producing lost completion until timeout despite quorum confirmation. This is a local correlation responsibility, not an asserted consensus-safety violation.

obligation.description: For each admitted remote ReadIndex request released by a same-term leader quorum confirmation, publication of its read index must retain that request's original SystemCtx and recipient identity, including when a later context confirms a queued prefix.

scope.description: Remote read-result identity at quorum prefix release in stable membership and authority; does not require eventual global progress.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine participants and authentic generated protocol messages
Distinct nonzero read contexts and legal message loss; no fabricated acknowledgments
Leader has committed an entry in its term before admitting queued reads
excluded: Membership changes or authority change during the measured release

grounding.derivation: The API returns a per-operation RequestState; local batches are keyed by SystemCtx. The prefix-confirmation test explicitly requires each returned status to retain its own context/origin, and the safe-read test compares ready context to originating context. Forwarding/readiness preserve wire context. Together these establish request identity preservation when consuming released statuses; they do not establish a time bound.
grounding.applicability: Multi-voter stable-term leader releases an admitted remote status after quorum confirmation, including a prefix confirmed by a later context.
alternatives: Sequential confirmations exercise only the same-context case; the required correlation also applies to earlier statuses in a released prefix.
